title: At Most One Inner Killing Horizon in Stationary Black Holes
summary: Stationary-axisymmetric black holes are the standard theoretical framework for astrophysical black holes, yet their interiors remain largely inaccessible: the absence of a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector renders the metric non-diagonal, and frame dragging obstructs the usual techniques for probing the interior. We prove that any stationary-axisymmetric black hole satisfying the classical energy conditions contains at most one nondegenerate inner Killing horizon per connected interior branch, irrespective of its matter content.
